sections.content: How many people stayed in Nottingham after gaining qualifications?

Nottingham is a city in the East Midlands. Nottingham also has a university.

Nottingham has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Nottingham ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 11,450 state-school pupils from Nottingham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 2,745 (24%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 2,880 (25%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Nottingham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Nottingham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Nottingham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Nottingham move to?

Of Nottingham's graduates, 790 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 235 of those graduates (30%) were living fairly locally, in the Nottingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Nottingham's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 690 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 415 of those qualified non-graduates (60%) were living fairly locally, in the Nottingham travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Nottingham's GCSE cohort:

  • 480 graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 185 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 60% of graduates and 35% of qualified non-graduates living in Nottingham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 4,800 graduates and 3,320 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Nottingham. This is compared with the 2,745 graduates and 2,880 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 40% of the graduates had also lived in Nottingham as GCSE pupils, while 60% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Nottingham in 2018 to 2019, 65% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 35% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
